name: Pick and roll: NBA reads
blurb: Giddey and Steve Nash: set up your man, read the coverage, then the low man, and let the defense tell you where the ball goes.

JG-PNR.t: How I See The Game as an NBA Player

TB-NASH.t: Steve Nash Breaks Down His Pick and Roll Mastery

m.title: Racing to the rim
m.q: You're past the screen and going to the rim. How do you finish?

choices.t: Reverse layup on the other side of the rim

m.ans: Two defenders are timing a block on his right hand, so he goes up and under for a reverse.
m.quote: As I go into my gather, you can see these guys are both trying to time a block, right? And the low man is kind of fanning out because he thinks Ingram's got it under control. So, as I go up for the layup, you can see I go for I take it to the other side on a reverse layup because Ingram and Scotty are both trying to block at the right-hand side.

m.title: Off the switch
m.q: You're coming downhill off the screen. Where does the ball go?
m.ans: LeBron's hands take away the wrap-around pass and Reaves still pulls in, so the corner is open with a long closeout.
m.quote: LeBron does a good job on the ball showing hands. He's kind of deterring that pass. And as LeBron starts to deter it, Reaves still pulls in, and that's when I go to my next read, which is Lonnie in the corner because there's no help. And as I pick the ball, you can see Reaves he gets two feet inside of the charge circle. So, it's a long closeout for him to get back out to the corner shooter.

m.title: Crowded paint
m.q: Eight players are in one corner of the floor. You want the ball to your screener. How?

choices.t: Go up like it's a layup, then drop it off
Bounce pass through the crowd now

m.ans: He shows the layup with his left hand, three defenders contest, and the drop-off is easy.
m.quote: So, my thought process here is show the layup. Is go up with my left hand, act like I'm shooting a layup. And you'll see as I go up with the left hand three guys contest, right? You got Podziemski, Santos, and Richards all down there contesting and it becomes an easy drop off to Sticks.

m.title: Middle ball screen
m.q: You have three teammates to choose from. Who gets it?

choices.t: The shooter on the far side

m.ans: The big steps up, the low man takes away the lob, so the weak-side shooter is the easy choice.
m.quote: So, my reads here are one is a lob to Rich. The second one, you got to pull behind Diakite who'll be pulling up the floor. The third one is Marciulionis. So, I act like I'm going to shoot a floater here, right? But I see Raymond steps up which kind of activates the low man here. He takes away the lob pass. So, now if you had to pick who was open here, Marciulionis is probably the easy choice.

m.title: Kept on the sideline
m.q: They're keeping you on the sideline. Where's the ball going?
m.ans: The low man inches out to the corner and the big commits to the ball, so the lob to the roller is easy.
m.quote: But, I'm watching him, right? And he thinks that as this play progresses bit by bit, you can see him start to inch out to the corner. So, he thinks Turner's got it under control. And as I see that, Green fans out, Kuzma fans out. This is a really easy lob throw to Rich.

m.title: Guard-guard screen
m.q: A guard comes to screen for you. What's your job?

choices.t: Be patient and read what the screener does
Go right away before the defense sets
Pass to the screener on the catch

m.ans: Wait for the screener to decide, then read it. They don't switch, so he gets downhill. His own fix: take one more dribble before picking it up.
m.quote: So, my job is to be patient and let Lenny make a decision whether he's going to screen, whether he's going to touch and roll, and kind of read him from there. So, I read what he does, and it allows me to get downhill. So, I probably picked the ball up way too early.

m.title: Two come at you
m.q: Two defenders come at you off the screen. Where does the ball go?

choices.t: Back to the screener popping out

m.ans: They trap him, so the popping big is open, and a teammate cutting out of the way leaves nobody to help.
m.quote: They put two on the ball. So, Six, who's a great shooter for us, he's our big that's going to pop here. I'm throwing this ball back to him and Isaac cuts out. So, as Isaac cuts, there's no one there. So, I throw it back to Six and it allows Six to get a wide open catch-and-shoot three.

m.title: Big diving down the middle
m.q: Your big is diving down the middle. Pass, shoot or drive?

choices.t: Pass to him for the short floater

m.ans: The big commits to the ball and the low man isn't high enough to stop it, so the pass to the diving big is wide open.
m.quote: Ayton commits to the ball, if you watch this. LaRavia is in a good low spot, but he's not high enough up the floor to deter a pass to Vuch, which as I throw this ball, it's a wide-open little floater for him.

m.title: Side pick and roll
m.q: Your man is behind you after the screen. What now?

choices.t: Get downhill and race him to the rim
Wait for him to catch up and reset
Pass to the screener right away

m.ans: His man had to chase over the screen and the big isn't switching, so he gets ahead and attacks.
m.quote: And Randle's not switching, Wells is chasing. So, they're kind of in a tough spot now, cuz it allows me to get ahead of steam downhill. It's just tough when you're playing behind the guy that's getting downhill.

m.title: Before the screen
m.q: You're bringing it up and the screen is coming. What do you do with your own man first?

choices.t: Get some space from him before the screen
Run him straight into the screen
Wait for the screener to come to you

m.ans: Loosen your man up so he's an arm's length or more away before you reach the screen. Then the big is isolated on you and has to commit.
m.quote: See how I've created that separation right there? The way I played, I thought this was extremely important. I didn't want my guy to be attached. If I could loosen my man up before I got to the screen where he was arms length or more. I just had such a big advantage because now I'm isolated on the big.

m.title: The big has to choose
m.q: You've walked your man into the screen. What's open?

choices.t: Whichever one the big doesn't take: the roller or your pull-up

m.ans: Your man is stuck on the screen, so the big can't play two. He has to commit to you or the roller, and you take the other.
m.quote: So, see, I'm isolated now on Damp, right? So, now Amari's got a role and Damp can't play the role. He's got to play me. Now, I've got both. I could have thrown this to Amari or I could take my pull-up.

m.title: Your man is still attached
m.q: The screen is there, but your man is still right on you. Come off it now?

choices.t: No, back up and set him up first
Yes, come off and attack the big

m.ans: He backs up with a hang dribble to threaten the middle, gets his man between the screener's feet, then comes off and attacks the space when his man goes under.
m.quote: So, like I could come off when Amari first offers the screen here, right? But he's he's in a good defensive position. So, when I see him start to go, I say, "M, I'm not creating any space here. Let me back up."

m.title: Two seven-footers up high
m.q: The big is up high and two seven-footers are above the free throw line. Use the screen?

choices.t: No, reject it and beat your own man into the open space

m.ans: Reject the screen and play one on one into the space behind them. If they all collapse, there are shooters everywhere.
m.quote: Damp's up. So I could come off and I could go try to go around damp, but they've got two sevenfooters above the free throw line. So my thought is let me just get by my defender and in that pocket of space.

m.title: Man on your back, big back
m.q: Your man is on your back and the big is staying with the roller. Not much space. What shot?
m.ans: If he pulls up he gets blocked from behind. Shoot it on the move so the trailing defender can't recover.
m.quote: But when I recognize he's on my back, I need to shoot this on the move so he can't recover and block this.

m.title: Corner empty, the big at the level
m.q: Corner empty, and the big is guarding the baseline. Where does it go?
m.ans: It's a pick-your-poison read on the big: if he plays the pocket, go by him baseline; if he respects the baseline, the pocket pass is there.
m.quote: If Durk tries to play the pocket, I'm going by him on the baseline. If he respects the baseline, the pocket's there,

m.title: Last defender at the rim
m.q: You've beaten two defenders and the last big has to come stop you. When do you pass to the roller?

choices.t: When his hips turn to you

m.ans: Take one more hard dribble to draw him. Once his hips turn, he can't get back to the roller.
m.quote: As soon as I see his hips turn, I know Amari's open.
